reason: The cited evidence (E2) directly supports that Al addition reduces density and increases specific strength in RHEAs, but provides no data on HfMoTaTiZr or on maintaining yield strength at 1000 °C. E1 discusses a different alloy system (HfMoNbTaTiZr) and does not address Al substitution, density reduction, or the specific baseline alloy. The key premises about preserving strength mechanisms and single-phase stability with Al in HfMoTaTiZr are unsupported by the cited passages.
premises: Al addition to RHEAs reduces density and increases specific strength
Partial Hf substitution with Al can maintain a single-phase BCC solid solution
Al acts as a substitutional solute that contributes to solid-solution strengthening
Lattice distortion and dislocation mechanisms responsible for high strength are preserved with moderate Al addition
The baseline HfMoTaTiZr alloy has density 10.21 g/cm³, ~1600 MPa RT yield strength, and ~855 MPa at 1000 °C
